classification.difficultyReason: Devise an unprompted symbolic angle chain: express an isosceles base angle in terms of the apex angle, transfer it into the right triangle, and use complementary angles to establish the half-angle relationship.

content.prompt:
$\triangle ABC$ is an isosceles triangle with $AB=AC$. $X$ is the point on $AC$ such that $BX$ is perpendicular to $AC$.

Prove that $\angle XBC=\frac12\angle BAC$.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle with A above B and C, double ticks on AB and AC, X on AC, and perpendicular BX. Ordinary source blue strokes are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC; X lies on AC; BX is perpendicular to AC. The right-angle square is in angle BXC.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and marks are permanent givens; no answer annotations.

answer.short:
$\angle XBC=90^\circ-\left(90^\circ-\frac12\angle BAC\right)=\frac12\angle BAC$.

Use equal base angles in $\triangle ABC$, then the angle sum of right-angled $\triangle BXC$.
answer.worked:
Since $AB=AC$, the base angles of $\triangle ABC$ are equal. Using its angle sum,
$$\begin{align*}
\angle ACB&=\frac{180^\circ-\angle BAC}{2}\\
\angle ACB&=90^\circ-\frac12\angle BAC.
\end{align*}$$
Since $X$ lies on $AC$, $\angle BCX=\angle ACB$. Also, $\angle BXC=90^\circ$. Using the angle sum of $\triangle BXC$,
$$\begin{align*}
\angle XBC&=90^\circ-\angle BCX\\
\angle XBC&=90^\circ-\left(90^\circ-\frac12\angle BAC\right)\\
\angle XBC&=\frac12\angle BAC.
\end{align*}$$
